items.title: About body alignment (your main goal)
items.body: General information, not a finding about your swimming. In competitive swimmers, trunk incline and the body's frontal area presented to the water both got smaller as swimming speed increased, and drag at a given speed depended mainly on that frontal area. (Zamparo et al., 2009) When swimmers were towed under water without moving, drag was lower with the head down or in line with the body than with the head up, by about 4 to 5% with the arms at the sides and about 10% with the arms stretched ahead. (Cortesi and Gatta, 2015) What AquaTrack can look at today: AquaTrack measures the body line, the legs against the trunk line and the head against the trunk line in the picture, and compares them with your own earlier swims filmed the same way. What it cannot: It does not judge these values as good or bad: its picture angles have not been checked against the measurements used in the research, and no target value has been verified.
limitations: Competitive swimmers at controlled speeds.
No threshold for an individual.
Passive towing, not swimming.
Ten experienced male swimmers.

items.title: About breathing
items.body: General information, not a finding about your swimming. A review of body roll research reports that swimmers roll the shoulders more than the hips, and that asymmetries in roll exist in front crawl without evidence that they affect performance. (Psycharakis and Sanders, 2010) What AquaTrack can look at today: Nothing yet. What it cannot: Breathing and body roll cannot be measured from an underwater side view, so AquaTrack reports nothing about your breathing.
limitations: The review itself lists many open questions.
Needs a front, overhead or multi-camera view.

items.title: Cycle time, start to end
items.body: The clip is too short to compare its start, middle and end: each third needs at least 3 reliable cycles (2 in the start, 3 in the middle, 2 in the end). What would help: A longer clip: at least nine full cycles of one arm.

items.title: Left-right balance
items.body: Needs both arms followed through whole pulls. From the side the far arm is hidden behind the body for part of every pull.

items.title: Arm coordination
items.body: Needs the start and end of both arms' pulls. The far arm's are hidden from a side view.

items.title: Kick rhythm
items.body: Kick beats are computed but have not been checked against video yet, and the far leg is often hidden.

items.title: Breathing timing
items.body: The head turn is not seen reliably from an underwater side view; the experimental detector has not been checked against video.

items.title: Body rotation
items.body: Rotation around the body's long axis cannot be measured from one side camera. It needs a front or overhead view.

items.title: Propulsion and efficiency
items.body: Force and efficiency cannot be measured from video of joint positions alone.

items.title: Change since earlier swims
items.body: This is a baseline: there is no earlier swim that can be compared with it. What would help: Another clip of the same distance and effort, filmed the same way.

items.title: Whether any value is good or bad
items.body: No reference values have been verified for these measurements, so nothing is compared with other swimmers or with an ideal.

checkpoints.title: Film the same swim again to see what changes
checkpoints.what_to_film: The same stroke and distance at the same effort, from the same place and angle as this clip.
checkpoints.compare_with: This swim, which is your baseline.
checkpoints.what_counts_as_a_change: A difference of more than about 4 degrees in body or leg line, 0.10 trunk lengths in head position, or 2 video frames in cycle time. Smaller differences are within measurement noise.
limitations: A difference shows that something changed, not why, and not whether it is better.
A sprint and an easy swim are not compared with each other.
